Both decision records are tracked and committed; no result refuted the siting, so no `**Amended by**` note was added anywhere.

memory_candidates.content: When a decision record names a measured precondition and the measurement comes back NOT refuting the ruling, the record that named the precondition still needs an edit -- but an `**Amended by**` note is the wrong marker, because nothing was amended. Use a distinct dated `**Discharged by** <record>, <date>:` note instead, and leave the record's own conditional rule ("if a measurement refutes the siting, the ruling is amended ... it is not worked around") verbatim, since discharge records that the measurement ran, it does not retire the rule for a future re-measurement. Verify the marker count via `git diff` rather than a raw `grep -c` on the phrase: a decision record can already carry an unrelated plain-text occurrence of the same words (e.g. a coverage table cell), inflating the count.

sapience_notes.subject: Claude Code harness: worktree outside the project directory
sapience_notes.value: File tools (Read/Write/Edit) proceed with no prompt or refusal for a path outside the project directory under bypassPermissions mode, but a registered content-validation PreToolUse hook still fires and can still block a Write/Edit there exactly as it would inside the project -- location does not bypass content gating.

sapience_notes.subject: Claude Code harness: path-scoped rules and external paths
sapience_notes.value: A session's .claude/rules/*.md paths: frontmatter glob does not match a file outside the project directory, even when the glob pattern matches the file's relative path. A live same-session A/B touch (external first, in-project second) of the identical glob showed no reminder for the external touch and an immediate one for the very next in-project touch -- ruling out dedupe as the explanation.

sapience_notes.subject: guard-destructive-git.sh hook anchoring
sapience_notes.value: A Bash-matched PreToolUse hook's safety decision (guard-destructive-git.sh) is anchored to the primary project tree's own git status, independent of the Bash command's own cd target. Measured by blocking a safe `git reset --hard HEAD` aimed at a provably clean external git worktree, because the unrelated primary tree was dirty -- the converse of the already-known defect where a destructive command aimed at a dirty worktree is wrongly allowed when the primary tree is clean. Both directions are one root mechanism, not two.

sapience_notes.subject: Dispatched subagent Bash tool cwd
sapience_notes.value: A dispatched subagent starts in the primary project directory, and its Bash tool's working directory resets between separate tool calls back to the primary project directory -- never to wherever a prior call's cd left it, and never to an external git worktree, even when a real external worktree exists for the whole measurement pass. Confirmed twice independently (this dispatch's own session, and a freshly spawned context-free general-purpose subagent given the same three-call pwd/cd/pwd sequence). A two-root design cannot rely on an ambient cwd switch; the worktree path must be carried explicitly.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh no-argument form
sapience_notes.value: Run with no arguments, verify-touched.sh derives touched paths from the whole working tree plus the committed diff against its own determined base, not just one task's own files -- so under a multi-task /orchestrate batch it naturally reflects every sibling task's concurrently dirty files, not a single task's declared file_scope. It can also run well past the harness's ~180s foreground-display auto-background threshold when many suites are selected (36 suites, 98 tests here), requiring a bounded kill -0 wait on the real OS PID rather than a tight shell timeout wrapper.

sapience_notes.subject: Decision-record discharge vs. amendment marker
sapience_notes.value: Closing a decision record's named precondition after a measurement that does NOT refute the ruling uses a distinct **Discharged by** <record>, <date>: marker, never **Amended by** -- the latter is reserved for when a measurement actually changes the ruling. Grep-based verification of marker counts should use git diff (what was actually added) rather than a raw grep -c on the phrase, since the phrase can already occur elsewhere in the file unrelated to the marker convention.
